I'm a hobbyist photographer that has started doing more and more work with cosplayers. I have a shoot coming up next week with a pair of WH40K cosplayers (one Sister of Battle and one Storm Warden) and wanted to do more than just studio portraits for them. Fortunately one of them is friends with the manager of the Games Workshop store in town and he let us take over one corner of the store on Saturday afternoon and shoot some of their painted miniatures. The challenge for me is to take those shots and make as believable as possible full size battle scene composite that I can also insert shots of the cosplayers into. This is a rough rendering throwing everything in and seeing what sticks just as a proof of concept that I'll be showing to the cosplayers before the shoot.

https://www.flickr.com/photos/elpeedee/18795726845/sizes/

I've been reliably informed that the Imperial Knight is way off scale (should be bigger), and shouldn't be fighting on the same side as Chaos Marines. The background sky and foreground are two separate shots composited, the planets were rendered from scratch using a texture I found through google. All completed in Photoshop CS6/Lightroom and using Knoll Light Factory and Color Efex Pro plugins.
